facts.label: Passado com that
facts.sub: We stayed at a hotel that had a pool. A woman that worked there helped us. Depois de that, o verbo vem logo, sem outro sujeito.

facts.label: Substantivo + that
facts.sub: Use that para dar informação sobre um lugar ou coisa: a hotel that had a pool, a room that opened onto a balcony. Em português, é o “que”. Depois de that vem o verbo, sem outro sujeito.

facts.label: Verbos no passado
facts.sub: Em lembranças, o verbo depois de that vai para o passado: had, cost, looked, opened, offered. Evite misturar: a hotel that had (não has) quando a história é do ano passado.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: That can start a description of a place.
We say “a hotel who had a pool” for things.
items.why: For things, say that or which.

items.s: For people, we can use who or that.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: That can start a description of a place. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “a hotel who had a pool” for things. → Falso (For things, say that or which.)
For people, we can use who or that. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Hotel memories in Glasgow · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy afternoon in Glasgow. Dee and Luisa drink tea in a small cafe. Last year they traveled to different places. Now they share stories about the hotels they stayed in. Luisa remembers a hotel that was funny and a little strange. Dee listens and asks many questions.
“Luisa, where did you stay last summer? Was it a good hotel?” says Dee. “We stayed at a hotel that had a pool on the roof.” says Luisa. “Wow! Was it a hotel that cost a lot of money?” says Dee.
